Passing a single file directly to M1 is not supported by the documented contract; the README says to put a single file in the directory if you have only one run per modality. Evidence about run_full_pipeline.sh accepting a single file does not establish that M1 accepts one, and no source states M1 accepts a single file directly.

rows.summary: No, randomise does not permit unrestricted permutations for repeated measurements. It restricts permutations to within exchangeability blocks defined by the group_labels option, so only observations sharing the same group label are exchanged. This accommodation is only sometimes possible, and correlated datasets generally violate null-hypothesis exchangeability.

rows.summary: No, randomise does not permit unrestricted permutations for repeated measurements. It allows the definition of exchangeability blocks via the group_labels option, so that only observations with the same group label are permuted within block. The applicability limitation is that permutation tests do not easily accommodate correlated datasets (e.g., temporally smooth timeseries) because such dependence violates null-hypothesis exchangeability; repeated measurements can sometimes be accommodated, but only with this block-based restriction.
